hypotheses: Fixed physical viscosity nu; smooth periodic divergence-free autonomous W imported from the companion source, with source-defined scaling-pulse neighborhood where W=(c(Z)(X-pi_1),-c(Z)(Y-pi_2),1).
N>=1 expanded compiler branches, B=2K+2>=14, scaling-slot midpoint z_r=(2N+r-1/2)/(5N), q_r=(pi_r.x,pi_r.y,z_r), and c(z_r)=-30N log B, from the protected actual-W witness.
Raw residual g=U_t+(U.grad)U-nu Delta U, U=alpha_1 W; projected force f=Pg=g-grad phi, Delta phi=div g, mean(phi)=0, projected pressure p=-phi.

new_mathematical_statement.exact_pressure_curvature: For every t>=1, Delta p_projected(t,q_r) = -1800*N^2*(log B)^2/(1+t)^2 < 0.
new_mathematical_statement.gauge_invariance: Every pressure representative p_projected+c(t) has the same nonzero Laplacian at q_r. Therefore no spatially constant (in particular zero) pressure can represent the same velocity U with a solenoidal forcing.
new_mathematical_statement.same_velocity_no_go: For any smooth pair (f,p) satisfying U_t+(U.grad)U = nu Delta U - grad p + f and div f=0 for this exact U, necessarily Delta p=-div g. At q_r and t>=1 this is strictly negative. Hence f solenoidal and grad p=0 are incompatible for the same U.
new_mathematical_statement.raw_force_allowed: The paper's separate raw general-force realization (g,0) is not contradicted: div g is allowed to be nonzero.

derivation: On the cutoff-one scaling-pulse neighborhood W=(c(Z)(X-pi_1),-c(Z)(Y-pi_2),1), so div W=0 and div[(W.grad)W]=tr[(DW)^2]=2c(Z)^2. The c'(Z) terms are present in DW but do not enter the trace of its square.
Because alpha depends only on t, div U_t=alpha' div W=0 and div Delta U=Delta div U=0. Therefore div g=alpha(t)^2 div[(W.grad)W]=2alpha(t)^2 c(Z)^2 on that neighborhood, independent of nu.
At q_r, c(z_r)=-30N log B; for t>=1, alpha_1(t)=1/(1+t). Thus div g(t,q_r)=1800 N^2 (log B)^2/(1+t)^2 > 0.
Taking divergence of g=-grad p+f with div f=0 gives Delta p=-div g. In particular Delta p(t,q_r) is the claimed negative expression; adding a function of t to p leaves this invariant.

For the paper's mean-zero projection phi, Delta phi=div g, f=g-grad phi, p=-phi. Hence the derived curvature is exactly the projected pressure's curvature; this is an identity, not a lower bound on a global norm.

import sympy as s
X,Y,Z,t,p1,p2,nu=s.symbols('X Y Z t p1 p2 nu', real=True)

coords=(X,Y,Z)
W=s.Matrix([c*(X-p1),-c*(Y-p2),1]); U=a*W
A=U.jacobian(coords)*U
G=U.diff(t)+A-nu*s.Matrix([sum(s.diff(U[i],z,2) for z in coords) for i in range(3)])

formal_correspondence.lean_fact: Pinned SlowFluidProperties demands solenoidal force and identically zero pressure for its own constructed U. The October actual W slow U cannot satisfy both demands with the same physical velocity and coordinates, by the gauge-invariant pressure curvature obstruction.
formal_correspondence.qualification: This is a conditional source-level same-velocity impossibility, not a contradiction with Lean: the Lean velocity is a different construction. It does not rule out arbitrary non-affine transformations or a separate Lean formalization of the projected formulation.
